papers.title: Spatio-temporal air flow properties in a 3D personalised model of the human lung
papers.abstract: We propose a multi-scale lung model to investigate spatio-temporal distributions of ventilation variables. Lung envelope and large airway geometries are derived from CT scans; smaller airways are generated using a physiologically consistent algorithm. Tissue mechanics is modeled using nonlinear elasticity under small deformations, coupled with local air pressure from fluid dynamics within the bronchial tree. Airflow accounts for inertia and static airway compliance. Simulations employ finite elements. Using this model, we explore spatio-temporal airflows and shear stresses distributions.

papers.title: GraphEP: A Calibrated Data System and Benchmark for Learning Cardiac Electrophysiology
papers.abstract: High-fidelity simulations generate spatiotemporal data that are difficult to obtain experimentally, yet their outputs are rarely ready for scientific machine learning. Cardiac electrophysiology (EP) exemplifies this challenge: data reside on anatomy-dependent volumetric meshes, propagation follows anisotropic material fields, and relevant events span multiple temporal scales. We introduce GraphEP, a calibrated data system that converts cardiac meshes and simulation protocols into compact, graph-native trajectories of full-field transmembrane potential. GraphEP includes 732 left-ventricular simulations across 20 anatomies, with healthy and scarred substrates of varying severity and multiple pacing configurations. Each sample provides geometry, tissue and material features, stimulation, connectivity, derived activation targets, and provenance in PyTorch Geometric format. We benchmark four inductive biases for predicting transmembrane potential Vm(t): local message passing, global neural operators, multi-scale hierarchical graph transformers (HGT), and physiology-informed models. The latter include HGT-Lag, which separates activation timing from action-potential morphology, and the stateful Graph Aliev-Panfilov Action-Potential ODE (GAP2ODE), which evolves excitation and recovery autoregressively with frame-wise stimulation and graph diffusion. Results show that wider spatial communication improves on local message passing, while physiological structure provides the strongest inductive bias: HGT-Lag and GAP2ODE lead on complementary metrics by explicitly modeling propagation, recovery, and temporal state. GraphEP offers a reproducible pathway from mechanistic cardiac EP simulations to analysis-ready data and a controlled benchmark for learning on irregular anatomical geometries.

papers.title: Morphological Features of Murine Pulmonary Arterial Networks for Diagnosing Vascular Disease
papers.abstract: Hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension results from prolonged time spent in a low-oxygen environment. The induced pulmonary hypertension leads to vascular remodeling, including vessel dilation and decreased compliance. This study aims to identify changes in vascular morphology in mice with pulmonary hypertension induced by hypoxia. To do so, we examine the pulmonary arterial network morphology using methods from geometry, topological data analysis, and statistical shape analysis. Tools from these fields are applied to arterial networks excised from micro-CT images of thirteen mice at four pressures. Networks from the hypertensive mice were normalized via a radius pruning algorithm, and analysis was conducted on the entire arterial network, as well as on a per-lobe basis. The main objective of this study was to present an adaptable pipeline for extracting features from micro-CT images to study how vascular disease affects arterial network morphology. Using this pipeline, we showed that the hypertensive mice have increased radius ratios and decreased length-to-radius ratios. Persistent homology analysis revealed that hypertension leads to lower branch-to-branch proximity and lower directional complexity in both the posterior and anterior directions. Persistence curves, particularly Betti curves, revealed lobe-specific differences in the left and inferior lobes. The first two shape principal component scores were also able to discriminate between control and hypertension at lower pressures. Importance metrics for each feature are computed using a boosted decision tree, and then an SVM classification model is fit with the most informative predictors for hypertensive classification.
